samples.summary: BoardToolbar's opt-in to the focus-release (hook call + `data-canvas-toolbar`) has no test
samples.evidence: The entire board-side change in this delta is wiring: `useCanvasFocusRelease()` at board-toolbar.tsx:137 and `data-canvas-toolbar=""` on `<Toolbar>` at :186. No test renders `BoardToolbar` at all — `board-toolbar-state.test.ts` only exercises `getToolbarState`/`canUngroupSelection` against stubs, and the hook's own suite (`toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx`) uses a synthetic `<div data-canvas-toolbar>` harness, never the real toolbar. If the attribute were dropped, misspelled, or swallowed by a component that did not spread props, nothing would fail: frontend has no `tsc` lane, and the attribute is an untyped string literal. The repo already has the pattern for this kind of assertion (`packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/toolbar-focus.test.ts` asserts `data-text-edit-keepalive` presence on rendered controls), so a rendered-attribute test is cheap and consistent.

samples.summary: The real-Radix "open trigger keeps focus" test was replaced by a static fixture that can never open a popup, so no test covers the production scenario
samples.evidence: The previous test clicked the real `DropdownMenuTrigger` ("Arrange"), waited for `role="menu"`, and asserted focus was not dropped out from under an open Radix menu. It is replaced (lines 67-75) by a click on a hard-coded `<button aria-expanded="true" data-state="open">Text color</button>` whose attributes are literals in the harness and never reflect any real popup state. That only exercises `hasOpenPopup()`'s attribute read; the actual behavior the comment claims ("blurring the trigger would close the popup the click just opened") is now untested against a real Radix trigger. The two remaining Radix tests (Escape at :95, menu item at :103) assert only the final released-to-body state, which stays true even if the hook wrongly blurred the trigger and collapsed the menu immediately after `findByRole("menu")` resolved — so the regression this test used to guard could ship green.

samples.summary: Keepalive exemption is only tested with the attribute directly on the button, not on an ancestor — the production shape
samples.evidence: `isReleasable` uses `el.closest(TEXT_EDIT_KEEPALIVE_SELECTOR)` (toolbar-focus-release.ts:76), i.e. ancestor matching. The new test fixture puts `data-text-edit-keepalive` on the button itself (line 48), so it would pass even if the implementation used `el.hasAttribute(...)`. Production usage is frequently on a wrapper: `font-size-picker.tsx:145` marks the wrapper `<div>` and `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/toolbar-focus.test.ts:195` asserts via `trigger.closest("[data-text-edit-keepalive]")`. The wrapper-marked case — the one the hook must honour for the font-size picker — has no coverage in this suite.

samples.summary: Pressed-toggle case uses a hand-written `data-state="on"` button rather than the real `Toggle` primitive
samples.evidence: The test at lines 77-83 relies on a fixture `<button data-state="on">Bold</button>` instead of the repo's actual `@/components/ui/toggle`, which is what real toolbars render (e.g. slides/board toggles). The assertion is meaningful (it fails if `hasOpenPopup` matched any `data-state`), but it encodes an assumption about Radix's attribute rather than exercising it; rendering the real `Toggle` in the harness would keep the guard honest if Radix changed its pressed-state attribute.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: BoardToolbar's focus-release opt-in (useCanvasFocusRelease() at board-toolbar.tsx:137 and data-canvas-toolbar="" on <Toolbar> at :186) has no test anywhere. Repo-wide grep for `canvas-toolbar`/`CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR` matches only the hook source, the hook's synthetic-div test harness (toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:25), the two production call sites, and docs. No test file imports BoardToolbar or board-view; board-toolbar-state.test.ts only exercises getToolbarState/canUngroupSelection against stubs and never imports the component. No e2e/playwright suite exists, and the frontend harness scripts (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs, verify-visual-browser.mjs, hunt-ui-runner.mjs) contain no reference to the attribute or a board-toolbar focus oracle; no test reads the source text either. Because the opt-in is an untyped data-* literal, a dropped/misspelled attribute or a non-spreading wrapper would break the behavior with zero test failures. The repo already has the exact assertion pattern for this (tests/components/text-formatting/toolbar-focus.test.ts asserts data-text-edit-keepalive on rendered controls), so this is a genuine missing-test gap on a shipped behavior change, not a "more coverage would be nice" nit.

finding.summary: The real-Radix "open trigger keeps focus" test was replaced by a static fixture that can never open a popup, so no test covers the production scenario
finding.evidence: The previous test clicked the real `DropdownMenuTrigger` ("Arrange"), waited for `role="menu"`, and asserted focus was not dropped out from under an open Radix menu. It is replaced (lines 67-75) by a click on a hard-coded `<button aria-expanded="true" data-state="open">Text color</button>` whose attributes are literals in the harness and never reflect any real popup state. That only exercises `hasOpenPopup()`'s attribute read; the actual behavior the comment claims ("blurring the trigger would close the popup the click just opened") is now untested against a real Radix trigger. The two remaining Radix tests (Escape at :95, menu item at :103) assert only the final released-to-body state, which stays true even if the hook wrongly blurred the trigger and collapsed the menu immediately after `findByRole("menu")` resolved — so the regression this test used to guard could ship green.

verdict.reason: The fixture test is not fake coverage: it fails if the behavior it claims to guard regresses. Traced execution of packages/frontend/src/components/toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:67-75 against the hook: the click's pointerdown sets pointerDriven (toolbar-focus-release.ts:99-101), focusin schedules the release timer (":119-122") BEFORE the test's own setTimeout(0) at test:71 (no fake timers — tests/setup.ts has none), and inside that timer isReleasable() (":71-79") passes every predicate (HTMLElement, inside [data-canvas-toolbar], tagName BUTTON, not keepalive) and is stopped ONLY by !hasOpenPopup (":59-64"). Break or remove hasOpenPopup and the trigger is blurred to body and the assertion at test:74 fails. So the assertion is discriminating, not true-regardless-of-behavior. The reviewer's framing that this "only exercises hasOpenPopup's attribute read" mistakes that read for a stub: the hook's entire production input is DOM attributes on document.activeElement — it never inspects Radix internals — and a real trigger that keeps focus while its popup is open exists in production (font-size-picker.tsx:196 uses onOpenAutoFocus={(e) => e.preventDefault()}), which is exactly what the fixture comment (test:34-36) models with the attributes Radix sets. A real uncontrolled DropdownMenuTrigger would NOT keep focus (Radix moves focus to the portalled content), which is a different code path — and that path IS covered: test:95-101 and test:103-108 drive the real DropdownMenu/Trigger/Item declared at test:28-33 through open→Escape and open→item-select, with test:106 requiring the real menu still mounted after the click. Nothing under test is mocked. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is at most a minor breadth gap (no explicit "menu still open" assertion), not a vacuous test or an untested behavior change, so it is not blocking.

finding.summary: "keeps focus on a trigger whose menu is open" does not exercise the open-popup guard — it passes even if `hasOpenPopup()` is deleted
finding.evidence: The test clicks the Radix `DropdownMenuTrigger`, then asserts only `document.activeElement !== document.body` and `trigger.getAttribute("data-state") === "open"`. Radix portals `DropdownMenuContent` to `document.body` and moves focus into it on open, so at the deferred `setTimeout` in `toolbar-focus-release.ts:103` `document.activeElement` is the portalled menu content, which fails `el.closest(TOOLBAR_SELECTOR) !== null` (line 58) long before `!hasOpenPopup(el)` (line 60) is ever consulted. Consequently `hasOpenPopup()` — including the deliberate exact-`"open"` comparison documented at toolbar-focus-release.ts:38-49 — has no test that can fail if it is wrong or removed. The second assertion (`data-state === "open"`) is also already implied by the preceding `await screen.findByRole("menu")`, so it re-asserts Radix's own state rather than the hook's behavior. The comment in the test ("either way the trigger must not be blurred") advertises coverage the assertions do not provide.

verdict.reason: The test described does not exist as characterized. The actual test (toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:67-75, "keeps focus on a trigger whose popup is open") does not click the Radix DropdownMenuTrigger — it clicks a plain in-toolbar button `<button aria-expanded="true" data-state="open">Text color</button>` (test file lines 37-39), so nothing is portalled and no focus is stolen; the `closest(TOOLBAR_SELECTOR)` short-circuit the finding relies on never occurs. The assertion is `expect(document.activeElement).toBe(trigger)`, not `!== document.body`, and there is no `data-state`/`findByRole("menu")` re-assertion in the test at all. Deleting `!hasOpenPopup(el)` from isReleasable (toolbar-focus-release.ts:71-79) makes that button satisfy every remaining clause, so the deferred callback at line 121 calls releaseFocusToBody, which blurs it (menu-focus.ts:68-72) and moves activeElement to document.body — failing the assertion. The exact-"open" comparison at lines 61-63 is separately pinned by "releases focus from a pressed toggle" (test lines 77-83), which clicks `data-state="on"` and requires focus to reach document.body. The guard is mutation-covered.

finding.summary: No test covers the documented `data-state="on"` (Radix Toggle) case, i.e. that a pressed toggle IS still released
finding.evidence: toolbar-focus-release.ts:38-49 states the `data-state` check compares against `"open"` exactly "because `Toggle` uses the same attribute for `on`/`off` and a pressed toggle must still be releasable" — the Bold/Italic-style buttons in the real slides toolbar. The harness (toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:22-36) contains only a plain `<button>`, an `<input>` and a dropdown; no element with `data-state="on"`/`aria-pressed`. If the comparison were loosened to `startsWith`/truthiness, every pressed toggle would silently stop releasing focus and the whole reported bug (#882) would return for toggles, with the suite still green.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists in the file the reviewer says they read in full. The harness at toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:40-44 renders `<button type="button" data-state="on">Bold</button>` (commented as a pressed Radix Toggle), and the test at lines 77-83, "releases focus from a pressed toggle", clicks it and asserts focus lands on document.body. Against the code under test (toolbar-focus-release.ts:59-64 `hasOpenPopup` exact-matching "open", consumed by `isReleasable` at 71-79), loosening the comparison to startsWith/truthiness — the exact mutation the finding describes as silently surviving — would make isReleasable return false for the Bold button, focus would stay on it, and this test would fail. The paired test at lines 67-75 exercises the `data-state="open"`/`aria-expanded="true"` side, so the two together pin the exact-match semantics. The finding's quoted evidence that the harness spans only lines 22-36 and contains only a button, an input and a dropdown is inaccurate: the harness runs to line 53 and includes the open-popup trigger, the pressed toggle and a keepalive control. Glob for **/toolbar-focus-release* returns exactly one test file, so no stale duplicate explains the discrepancy.
